battle.name: 第七次反法同盟
battle.theater: 滑鐵盧與沙勒羅瓦戰場
battle.brief: 一八一五年三月，拿破崙自厄爾巴島潛返法國，維也納列強組成第七次同盟，戰事在六月集中於布魯塞爾以南的滑鐵盧。英荷聯軍死守威靈頓的高地線，普軍依布魯厄爾由東南壓上；法軍在午後暴雨中火藥受潮、步槍難以擊發而潰散。火繩槍銃此時已退居二線，只剩火繩點火的老法子留在高地團手裡。

kit.name: 火繩槍銃
kit.history: 比步槍輕的長槍。西班牙人帶著它上船，也帶著它進了美洲。

countries: 第七次同盟是拿破崙脫離厄爾巴島之後，維也納會議列強重新合圍法國的軍事聯盟。同盟本體是七個君主國：俄羅斯帝國、普魯士王國、奧地利帝國、大不列顛王國、瑞典王國、西班牙王國與葡萄牙王國，此外還有荷蘭聯合王國，以及一批被維也納會議重新編排的德意志邦國——漢諾威、拿騷、符騰堡、巴伐利亞、黑森與奧爾登堡等，各以主力團、邦軍或民兵的形式加入聯軍。法國一方是重建的法蘭西帝國與其附庸：萊茵同盟殘餘邦的分遣隊、那不勒斯王國穆雷的騎兵、薩丁王國的部隊與波蘭軍團。聯軍沒有單一的戰場指揮：政治與戰略決策握在維也納會議四大國代表（英、俄、普、奧）手中，軍事上分為三個互不隸屬的戰區——威靈頓公爵在布魯塞爾指揮英、荷與比利時聯軍總部，布魯厄爾在沙勒羅瓦與利尼一帶指揮普軍總部，俄軍與奧軍分別在波蘭戰線與南德戰線承擔次要壓力，皇家海軍負責封鎖法國海岸與護送聯軍在本土集結。拿破崙把在役老兵重新編為北方軍、中部軍、南方軍與西部軍，內伊領北方軍，格魯希掌騎兵與第三軍，埃爾金領第四軍，波拿波領波蘭軍，全部作戰由拿破崙直接指揮，沒有一個軍團可以自行決定戰役方向。
countriesEn: The Seventh Coalition was the military alliance through which the powers of the Congress of Vienna closed in on France again after Napoleon left Elba. Its core was seven monarchies: the Russian Empire, the Kingdom of Prussia, the Austrian Empire, the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, the Kingdom of Sweden, the Kingdom of Spain and the Kingdom of Portugal, joined by the United Kingdom of the Netherlands and by a set of German states newly redrawn by the Congress — Hanover, Nassau, Württemberg, Bavaria, Hesse and Oldenburg among them — which entered the war as line battalions, contingents of their own, or militia. On the French side stood the reconstituted French Empire with its satellites: detachments from the rump states of the Confederation of the Rhine, the cavalry of Murat's Kingdom of Naples, the troops of the Kingdom of Sardinia and the Polish corps. The Allies had no single field command. Political and strategic decisions belonged to the plenipotentiaries of the four great powers at the Congress (Britain, Russia, Prussia and Austria), while in the field the war divided into three independent theatres: the Duke of Wellington commanding the Anglo-Dutch-Belgian headquarters at Brussels, Blücher commanding the Prussian headquarters around Charleroi and Ligny, the Russians and the Austrians applying secondary pressure on the Polish and South German lines, and the Royal Navy blockading the French coast and carrying the Allied contingents to their assembly areas. Napoleon rebuilt his old soldiers into an Army of the North, an Army of the Centre, an Army of the South and an Army of the West. Ney led the North, Grouchy held the cavalry and the III Corps, d'Erlon the IV Corps and Poniatowski the Polish corps. Every battle was directed by Napoleon himself, and not one corps was allowed to decide the direction of a campaign on its own.
people: 拿破崙一世是這場戰爭唯一真正的中心。百日王朝整個存在只為他一人：他從厄爾巴島逃回法國，在巴黎重新加冕，率軍北上，最後在滑鐵盧把全部兵力押上右翼，分兩路同時進攻，午後暴雨令火藥受潮仍照令進攻，黃昏又發動大規模騎兵衝鋒，結果全軍在自己的火力和泥濘裡散掉。威靈頓公爵是英荷聯軍的樞紐，他選擇反向斜坡的防禦位置，把英軍師、蘇格蘭高地團、荷蘭與比利時部隊編在同一條山脊上，午後遭內伊密集衝鋒仍不換位，直到普軍出現在地平線上才下令總反攻。普軍元帥布魯厄爾在利尼與沙勒羅瓦牽制格魯希後按計畫西行，傍晚不待全軍集結便釋放正面兵力，令第一軍與第四軍接連攻入法軍右翼；普軍參謀長格奈森瑙則在後方策應行軍與補給。內伊因動作失當而受詬病，他未等埃爾金的步兵縱隊展開便驅騎兵衝鋒，兩次大規模騎兵攻擊都撞在英軍的方陣上；埃爾金遲疑遲遲，第四軍直到午後才投入正面；格魯希在利尼的膽怯，使普軍得以趕到滑鐵盧；波拿波的波蘭軍在右翼被消耗殆盡。英軍第 92 師的戈登上尉與高地團的老兵們，在雨裡靠火繩點火守住英軍右翼；普軍第 17 團「冷血」第 3 營由麥塞爾巴赫中校率領，率頭髮上滴著雨的士兵衝入法軍右翼的炮兵陣地。維也納會議那一邊，真正決定法國命運的是梅特涅、卡斯勒雷與沙皇亞歷山大一世，而不是滑鐵盧上的任何一名將領。
peopleEn: Napoleon I was the single true centre of this war. The Hundred Days existed for him alone: he fled Elba and returned to France, crowned himself again in Paris, marched north, and at Waterloo committed every man he had to the right-hand side, attacking on both wings at once, ordering the advance in the afternoon even though the rain had spoiled his cartridges, and then launching his great cavalry charge at dusk, only to see his army dissolve in its own firepower and in the mud. The Duke of Wellington was the hinge of the Anglo-Dutch-Belgian army. He chose the reverse-slope position, drew the British divisions, the Scottish Highland regiments and the Dutch and Belgian units along a single ridge, and refused to shift his line through the afternoon despite Ney's repeated mounted attacks, ordering the general counter-attack only when the Prussians appeared on the horizon. Field Marshal Blücher, having held Grouchy at Ligny and Charleroi, marched west according to plan and, in the evening, released his leading troops before his whole army had closed up, sending the I and IV Corps in succession into the French right flank; General Gneisenau handled the marching columns and the supply arrangements behind him. Ney was the object of criticism for his handling of the attack, for he launched the cavalry without waiting for d'Erlon's infantry to deploy, and his two massed charges of horse broke on the British squares. d'Erlon was slow, and his IV Corps did not enter the line until the afternoon; Grouchy's hesitation at Ligny allowed the Prussians to reach the field; and Poniatowski's Polish corps was ground down on the right. Captain Gordon of the 92nd and the old men of the Highland regiments held the British right through the rain by lighting their charges with matches, while Lieutenant-Colonel Massenbach led the third battalion of the 17th Regiment, the Cold Blood, through the rain into the French artillery position on the right flank. On the other side of the table at the Congress of Vienna, the men who decided France's fate were Metternich, Castlereagh and Tsar Alexander I, and not one of the generals at Waterloo.
kits: 火繩槍銃在本場戰爭中的位置很特別：它已經不是前線武器，而是殘餘。一八一五年的歐洲正規軍早已全面改裝燧發滑膛槍——英軍是口徑約 0.54 吋的「褐貝絲」燧發槍，配一七九八年制式刺刀；法軍是 1777 年式滑膛槍；奧軍是 1809 年式燧發步槍；俄軍、荷軍與比軍也一律用燧發槍。火繩槍銃比步槍輕得多，槍身短、槍口約二十幾公厘，重量只有步槍的一半，卻射程近、射速慢、在雨天極不可靠，所以十六世紀的西班牙人與義大利人把它帶上船隊、帶進美洲的灘頭；到一八一五年，它只剩下三個位置：第一，各國軍械庫與要塞守備的舊械，以及殖民地與邊防分遣隊的常備槍械，例如俄軍克里米亞與高加索線的守備營、西班牙在美洲殖民地與本國第二線的舊槍；第二，預備役與民兵手中的淘汰舊槍，荷蘭與比利時民兵多帶獵槍與長矛，西班牙與葡萄牙的第二線民兵仍握著上世紀末的舊式火槍；第三，也是本戰役裡唯一真正看得見的痕跡，就是「用火繩點火」這個法子。六月十八日下午暴雨，紙包的火藥浸濕，燧發槍的燧石打著火也燒不起來，英軍第 42 師「黑巴士」、第 92 師等高地團改用火繩與火柴點燃引火盤——那正是火繩槍銃的射擊程序，只是手裡握的已是新式槍。戰場上的主力裝備另有各軍制式步槍與刺刀，英軍的 1796 年式輕騎兵刀與騎兵卡賓槍，普軍獵兵的雷管槍以及仍列裝於部分普魯士火槍兵手中的火繩步槍，法軍的 12 磅「紐斯」野戰炮、4 磅「獨腿」炮、騎炮兵，以及伏兵使用的雷管小槍；再加上圍城用的重炮、壕溝工具與攻城槌，以及把聯軍補給從英吉利海峽運上陸的船隻與馬車。
kitsEn: The place of the arquebus in this war is peculiar: it was no longer a front-line weapon but a remnant. By 1815 the regular armies of Europe had gone over completely to flintlock muskets — the British carried the 0.54 inch Brown Bess with the 1798 pattern bayonet, the French the 1777 pattern musket, the Austrians the 1809 pattern flintlock, and the Russians, Dutch and Belgians likewise flintlocks. The arquebus was far lighter than a musket, with a short barrel of some twenty-odd millimetres across the bore and about half the weight of a musket, but it had short range, slow rate of fire and was hopeless in the rain, which is why sixteenth-century Spaniards and Italians took it aboard their ships and into the beachheads of the Americas. By 1815 it survived in only three places: first, as old service weapons in depots and garrisons, and as the standing arms of colonial and frontier detachments such as the Russian garrison companies in the Crimea and the Caucasus, the Spanish colonial and second-line formations in Spain and its American possessions; second, as obsolete guns in the hands of reservists and militia, with the Dutch and Belgian militia carrying hunting guns and pikes and the Spanish and Portuguese second lines still holding late sixteenth-century matchlocks and older flintlocks; third — and the only trace of it actually visible on the battlefield of this war — the practice of firing from a match. From the afternoon of 18 June the rain soaked the paper cartridges, and a flintlock struck true would not catch; the 42nd Foot, the Black Watch, and the 92nd and other Highland regiments fell back on matches and slow match to light the priming pan. That was the firing drill of the arquebus, though the weapon in their hands was now a new-pattern musket. The rest of the material on the field was the standard muskets, bayonets, the 1796 pattern light cavalry sword and cavalry carbines of the British, the percussion guns of the Prussian jägers and the match muskets still carried by some Prussian musketeer regiments, the French 12-pounder obusiers, 4-pounder pieces, horse artillery and the small percussion carbines of the voltigeurs, together with heavy guns, trench tools and siege hammers for the blockade, and the ships and wagons that carried the Allied supplies from the English Channel ashore.
tactics: 威靈頓在滑鐵盧北面的緩坡上拉了一條反向斜坡防線：西端是拉艾聖，中段是拉海與聖讓山，東端是帕佩洛特與于貢蒙農莊，英軍方陣正面朝北，步兵以密集縱列站到坡頂的反斜面上，讓法軍在平原上的視線只能看見零星散兵，己方卻能把整齊的火力一路壓下來。拿破崙的計畫是兩翼同時壓上：北面右翼由內伊的步兵與法軍工兵猛攻拉艾聖，再以奈伊的騎兵大舉衝鋒拉海與帕佩洛特之間的高地；南面左翼由埃爾金的第四軍加波拿波的波蘭軍攻于貢蒙與帕佩洛特。自午後兩時起暴雨，坡地變成泥濘，法軍縱隊的射速與機動大減，英軍火藥受潮後射擊更慢，交鋒節奏整個被拖垮。真正的轉折出現在地平線上：布魯厄爾的普軍擺脫格魯希，午後四時起以密集縱隊自東南壓上，先鋒第 17 團第三營一度被法軍擋回，經炮火支援再攻，奪下拉艾聖外側與法軍右翼的炮兵陣地，把法軍的倒 V 形陣線拉成兩截。英軍趁勢全線反攻，法軍最後一次大規模騎兵反擊被普軍方陣擋住，天黑之後法軍崩散，聯軍連夜追擊，皇家海軍封鎖法國北部港口，普軍越過邊界向巴黎推進；維也納會議隨後在七月頒布最後宣言，第二次開戰，把法軍逼回本土。
tacticsEn: Wellington drew a reverse-slope line along the gentle rises north of Waterloo: La Haye Sainte at the western end, La Haye and Mont-Saint-Jean in the middle, Papelotte and the Hougoumont farm at the eastern end. The British squares faced north, the infantry stood in close columns on the reverse of the crest, so that the French on the plain could see only a few skirmishers while the whole weight of the volley came down on them. Napoleon's plan was to press on both wings at once: on the right to the north, Ney's infantry and the French engineers drove hard at La Haye Sainte, and then Ney's cavalry was thrown in as a massed charge against the heights between La Haye and Papelotte; on the left to the south, d'Erlon's IV Corps and Poniatowski's Poles attacked Papelotte and the Hougoumont farm. From two in the afternoon the rain came down, the slope turned to mud, the rate of fire and the mobility of the French columns fell away, and with his cartridges spoiled the British shot more slowly still, so that the whole rhythm of the engagement was dragged out. The real turn came on the horizon: Blücher shook off Grouchy and from four in the afternoon pressed in dense columns from the south-east, the third battalion of the 17th being checked at first, then carried forward under covering fire to take the outer edge of La Haye Sainte and the French artillery on the right flank, tearing the French inverted V in two. The British counter-attacked along the whole line, the last great French cavalry stroke was stopped by the Prussian squares, and after dark the French army dissolved, the Allies pursued through the night, the Royal Navy blockaded the northern French ports, and the Prussians crossed the frontier toward Paris. The Congress of Vienna followed with its final declaration in July, renewing the war and driving the French back into their own country.
data: 滑鐵盧正面的兵力大致相當：法軍在陣地上約五萬三千人，聯軍在陣地上約六萬八千人，其中英荷與比利時部隊約五萬二千，普軍可投入的兵力約五萬，其中先頭部隊在當日午後才趕到。整場戰鬥自凌晨兩時法軍以炮火打開序幕，到入夜法軍潰散，延續十三個小時以上；六月那場暴雨自午後兩時起下了約五小時，坡地泥濘終日未乾。傷亡方面，聯軍損失普遍被估在二萬二千人上下：英軍死傷與失散合計約一萬三千人，普軍約六千人，荷蘭與比利時部隊約三千人；法軍陣亡、受傷與失散合計三萬五千至四萬人，被聯軍看管俘獲者約八千人，其中大半是傷兵與掉隊的老兵。距離上，滑鐵盧距布魯塞爾約二十公里，普軍主力自利尼與沙勒羅瓦向西行軍十五至二十公里才接上戰線；法軍右翼與英軍左翼的接觸點在帕佩洛特，距英軍中段約一公里；英軍右翼拉艾聖距拿格爾陣亡處不到一公里半。補給上，英軍自六月十六日起由英吉利海峽的港口運來約五天份乾糧與火藥，法軍隨身麵包只夠一天半，飲水靠戰地井泉，午夜的火藥補充線因雨受阻，紙包火藥大量作廢，聯軍在布魯塞爾與奧斯特龍一線的軍需倉儲多被雨浸透，只能靠木箱保護；當晚法軍丟棄的炮車與帳篷數量可從聯軍繳獲清冊上見到，僅拉艾聖一線就收得法軍砲車十數門。
dataEn: The numbers facing each other at Waterloo were close. The French had about fifty-three thousand men in the line, the Allies about sixty-eight thousand, of whom some fifty-two thousand were British, Dutch and Belgian and about fifty thousand Prussians were available, the leading detachments of the latter arriving only in the afternoon of the 18th. The fighting ran from the French opening with gun at two in the morning until the French broke up after dark, more than thirteen hours in all, and the rain of June fell for roughly five hours from two in the afternoon, leaving the slope churned and wet from end to end. In losses the Allies are commonly reckoned at about twenty-two thousand: roughly thirteen thousand British dead, wounded and missing, about six thousand Prussians and about three thousand Dutch and Belgians; the French dead, wounded and missing together came to between thirty-five and forty thousand, with about eight thousand taken prisoner, most of them wounded men and stragglers. As for distances, Waterloo lies about twenty kilometres from Brussels, and the Prussian columns marched fifteen to twenty kilometres west from Ligny and Charleroi before they could make contact; the point where the French right and the British left met was at Papelotte, some kilometre from the centre of the British line, and the British right at La Haye Sainte lay under a kilometre and a half from the spot where Nagle was wounded. On supply: from 16 June the British brought up about five days of rations and powder over the English Channel, the French carried barely a day and a half's bread, drew water from the wells on the field, and the midnight ammunition column was checked by the rain, so that large numbers of paper cartridges were spoiled; the Allied depots at Brussels and Ostend were soaked through and could only be protected in wooden cases. The French guns and baggage abandoned that night show up in the Allied capture lists, La Haye Sainte alone accounting for a dozen or more captured French guns.
cause: 戰爭的直接起因是拿破崙在厄爾巴島上的去留。維也納會議在1814 年到 1815 年初重新分割歐洲，把法國限制在一七九二年的邊界，荷蘭王國合併比利時，聯軍計畫在法國北部駐紮三年，並派奧地利軍進駐法國邊境；會議同時把拿破崙流放到厄爾巴島，等於以實力廢黜他。拿破崙在島上不得自由行動，也難以得知會議的實際內容，待訪客與英方專員帶來消息，確認維也納準備把法國壓回舊疆界，他於一八一五年三月七日帶近千人分乘數條小船渡海，三月十三日在法國南岸登陸，沿途受地方官員與民眾歡迎而未被攔截，三月二十日進入巴黎，重新登上皇位，開始百日王朝。這個動作立刻把維也納會議正在編排的歐洲秩序推到懸崖邊：會議宣告拿破崙為敵人，七國在四月組成第七次同盟，奧地利對法宣戰，聯軍在五月完成動員，六月渡過萊茵河並在法國北部集結完畢。對法國人而言，起因還多一層：拿破崙帶回舊法軍的旗幟與革命軍的傳統，也帶回一段國民性的驕傲；對聯軍而言，這是一場防止法國再起、並徹底終結它的行動，而維也納會議對法國邊界、荷蘭王國與波蘭問題的處理，正是把各國推向戰爭的真正理由。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the war was the question of what was to be done with Napoleon on Elba. Between 1814 and early 1815 the Congress of Vienna redrew Europe: France was to be confined within her 1792 borders, the Kingdom of the Netherlands was to absorb Belgium, the Allies planned to garrison the north of France for three years, and Austrian troops were moved up to the French frontier. At the same time the Congress banished Napoleon to Elba, which was to be a forcible removal from power. On the island he was denied freedom of movement and found it hard to learn what the Congress had actually decided; when visitors and British emissaries brought word that Vienna meant to push France back inside her old frontiers, he crossed the Channel in a flotilla of small boats with a few hundred men on 7 March 1815, landed on the south coast of France on the 13th, was welcomed by local officials and crowds all the way north without being intercepted, and entered Paris on 20 March to resume the throne and open the Hundred Days. The move at once pushed the European order the Congress was assembling to the edge of a cliff: the Congress declared Napoleon an enemy, the seven powers formed the Seventh Coalition in April, Austria declared war, the Allies completed their mobilisation in May, and in June crossed the Rhine and assembled in the north of France. For the French there was a further layer to the cause: Napoleon brought back the banners of the old army and the traditions of the revolutionary army, and with them a national pride. For the Allies it was an action to prevent France from rising once more and to finish the business entirely, and it was the Congress's settlement of the French frontier, of the Kingdom of the Netherlands and of Poland that supplied the real reason for the states to go to war.
impact: 滑鐵盧之後的一八一五年到一八一八年，是歐洲保守秩序重新固化的三年。維也納會議於一八一五年六月九日簽署最終法案，確立以奧地利主持的中歐均勢、俄國在東歐的仲裁地位、普魯士在萊茵的擴張，以及包含比利時的荷蘭王國所代表的北方版圖；九月十四日俄、奧、普三國君主結成像一八一二年同盟那樣的協作安排，後來擴大為神聖同盟，並由英國、西班牙與瑞典等國先後加入。法國則第二次被削弱：一八一五年十一月二十日的巴黎條約把法國退回一七九二年的邊界，法軍被限制在十萬人以下，法國支付七千萬法郎賠款，聯軍在法國北部駐紮三年直到一八一八年，普魯士得到萊茵省與萊茵聯邦的部分領土，荷蘭王國取得原奧屬的低地國家。但保守秩序並沒有解決自由與民族主義的問題：西班牙、義大利、德意志邦國與巴爾幹的騷動在一八一五年到一八二〇年代接連爆發，一八二〇年的西班牙自由革命與此後法國的兩次王朝更替，都說明滑鐵盧解決的是戰爭，而不是政治。滑鐵盧從此成為歐洲軍事史上的座標，此後一百多年裡，每逢歐洲大軍動員，人們都會拿它來作比。
impactEn: The three years from 1815 to 1818 were the years in which the conservative order of Europe hardened once more after Waterloo. On 9 June 1815 the Congress of Vienna signed its Final Act, fixing the Austrian-centred balance in central Europe, the arbitrating position of Russia in the east, the Prussian extension into the Rhineland, and the northern map represented by the Kingdom of the Netherlands with Belgium inside it. On 14 September the monarchs of Russia, Austria and Prussia entered into an arrangement of the same kind as the Quadruple Alliance of 1812; it was later widened into the Holy Alliance and joined in turn by Britain, Spain and Sweden. France was diminished for the second time: the Treaty of Paris of 20 November 1815 returned her to the frontiers of 1792, limited her army to a hundred thousand men, imposed an indemnity of seventy million francs, and kept Allied troops garrisoned in the north of France until 1818; Prussia received the Rhine province and part of the Confederation of the Rhine, and the Kingdom of the Netherlands received the former Austrian lowland possessions. But the conservative order did not solve the questions of liberty and nationality: unrest in Spain, Italy, the German states and the Balkans broke out in an unbroken series from 1815 to the 1820s, and the liberal revolution in Spain in 1820 and the two subsequent changes of dynasty in France showed that Waterloo had settled a war, not a political problem. Waterloo became a fixed point in the military history of Europe, and for more than a century afterwards every general mobilisation on the continent was measured against it.
result: 六月十八日入夜，法軍的陣線在中央與右翼相繼瓦解，埃爾金的縱隊被切斷，拉艾聖與帕佩洛特兩端的守軍自行撤退，格魯希與埃爾金收攏殘部退向沙勒羅瓦與法國境內，普軍追過邊境，拿破崙的退路就此斷掉。他回到巴黎，維也納會議不接受任何交換條件，宣布法國為敵國，七月聯軍第二次開戰，七月底聯軍進入巴黎，六月二十二日拿破崙再次退位，這一次被押送至英屬聖赫勒拿島，於一八一五年十二月抵達，終老島上。一八一五年七月至九月，聯軍分別進駐法國北部與比法邊境的要點，巴黎被佔領至一八一八年十一月。一八一五年十一月二十日簽訂第二次巴黎條約，法國正式接受歐洲列強劃定的邊界與賠款安排，支付七千萬法郎並分三期繳納，割讓安科爾等處，一八一六年三月生效。聯軍司令部同時解散，軍隊陸續回國。結果是拿破崙時代的歐洲戰爭在滑鐵盧正式收場：法國退守本土，海陸兩面的封鎖解除，維也納體系取得三十年的相對穩定，直到一八三〇年的革命浪潮再度把它沖垮。
resultEn: On the night of 18 June the French line came apart in the centre and on the right, d'Erlon's columns were cut off, the garrisons at La Haye Sainte and Papelotte gave themselves up, and Grouchy and d'Erlon gathered what was left of their men and fell back toward Charleroi and the French border with the Prussians in pursuit, so that Napoleon's road was cut. He returned to Paris; the Congress of Vienna accepted no terms and declared France an enemy; the war was renewed in July, the Allies entered Paris at the end of that month, and on 22 June Napoleon abdicated a second time, this time to be carried to the British island of Saint Helena, where he arrived in December 1815 and remained for the rest of his life. Between July and September 1815 the Allies occupied the principal points of the north of France and of the Franco-Belgian border, and Paris stayed under occupation until November 1818. On 20 November 1815 the Second Treaty of Paris was signed: France formally accepted the frontiers and the indemnity laid down by the European powers, undertook to pay seventy million francs in three instalments, and ceded places such as Ancona, the treaty taking effect in March 1816. The Allied command was dissolved at the same time and the armies went home. In the end the European war of the Napoleonic age closed formally at Waterloo: France was confined to her own country, the blockade by sea and land was lifted, and the Vienna system bought about thirty years of relative stability, until the revolutionary tide of 1830 broke over it again.
